label: Reliance on chance variation and natural selection stalls inquiry into physical causes
candidate_data: none known

label: Cells, tissues, shells, bones, leaves and flowers are shaped by the laws of physics
measurable_quantities: cell and tissue shape; mechanical stresses and surface tensions in tissues; shell and bone geometry
candidate_data: Cell and tissue shape imaging datasets (Allen Cell Explorer, Image Data Resource) paired with published tissue mechanics measurements; 3D morphology scans in MorphoSource.

label: Problems of organic form are mathematical and problems of growth are physical
candidate_data: none known

label: No known physical law is transgressed by the bodily mechanism
measurable_quantities: energy and mass balance of organisms; osmotic and surface forces in tissues
candidate_data: Whole-organism calorimetry and energy-balance studies and published physiological measurements of osmosis and membrane transport.

section: Form as a diagram of forces
label: The form of an object is a diagram of the forces acting or that have acted on it
measurable_quantities: shape of cells or skeletal elements; measured or inferred mechanical stresses and forces
candidate_data: Studies inferring cell and tissue forces from shape (cell-shape image datasets such as the Image Data Resource) and finite-element analyses of bone built on MorphoSource scans.

label: Surface tension at a cell's boundary strongly affects its form
measurable_quantities: cell surface or cortical tension; cell shape and curvature; composition of surrounding medium
candidate_data: Published micropipette and atomic-force-microscopy measurements of cell cortical tension alongside cell-shape images (Image Data Resource).

label: Protoplasm behaves as a highly viscous fluid that changes shape under force
measurable_quantities: cytoplasmic viscosity; deformation rate under applied pressure
candidate_data: Published microrheology and micropipette-aspiration measurements of cytoplasmic viscosity in amoebae and other cells.

label: Vital phenomena cannot be cleanly divided into physical and non-physical ones
candidate_data: none known

label: Nuclei, chromosomes and germ-plasm act only as seats of energy and centres of force
candidate_data: none known

label: Changes in the length-weight constant k reveal changes of form during growth
measurable_quantities: body length; body weight; length-weight coefficient k across growth
candidate_data: Length-weight relationship parameters compiled in FishBase and fisheries survey length-weight records.

label: Tree trunk diameter must grow as the 3/2 power of height
measurable_quantities: trunk diameter at base; tree height; maximum height per species
candidate_data: Tree height-diameter allometry databases such as Tallo, national forest inventory data, and TRY plant traits for wood density and maximum height.

label: Gravity sets an upper limit on the size of terrestrial animals
measurable_quantities: body mass; limb-bone cross-sectional area or circumference; muscle cross-sectional area
candidate_data: Published compilations of limb-bone circumference and body mass across mammals, 3D bone scans in MorphoSource, and body masses from PanTHERIA.

label: Buoyancy removes the physical barrier to size in fully aquatic animals
measurable_quantities: maximum body mass of aquatic versus terrestrial lineages; body density
candidate_data: Body-mass compilations for mammals (PanTHERIA) and fossil body-size records in the Paleobiology Database comparing aquatic and terrestrial maxima.

label: Larger fish can sprint faster but cover similar distances and tire more slowly
measurable_quantities: burst swimming speed; sustained swimming speed or endurance; annual distance travelled; body length; gill or lung surface area; metabolic rate
candidate_data: Published swimming-performance datasets (burst and critical swimming speeds), animal telemetry tracking records, and metabolic-rate data in AnAge and AnimalTraits.

label: Power needed for flight grows as length^3.5 while muscle power grows as length^3
measurable_quantities: body length or mass; minimum and cruising flight speed; flight muscle mass; power required for flight
candidate_data: Published bird flight-speed measurements (e.g. radar and tracking studies), flight-muscle mass compilations, and body masses from AnimalTraits.

label: Ostrich and moa have passed the size at which muscular flight is possible
measurable_quantities: body mass; flight muscle mass; maximum mass of flying birds
candidate_data: Body-mass compilations of extant and extinct birds (AnimalTraits; Paleobiology Database for fossil taxa) with flight ability recorded.

section: Giant fossil fliers and air density
label: Giant Carboniferous insects and pterodactyls imply a denser ancient atmosphere
measurable_quantities: fossil wingspan; body size; reconstructed atmospheric density or composition through time
candidate_data: Fossil insect and pterosaur size records in the Paleobiology Database and published geochemical reconstructions of Phanerozoic atmospheric CO2 and O2.

label: Similarly built animals should jump to the same absolute height regardless of size
measurable_quantities: jump height; take-off velocity; body mass; jumping muscle mass; limb lever length
candidate_data: Published comparative jumping-performance datasets across insects, frogs and mammals with body mass.

label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
measurable_quantities: locomotor speed; body length; leg length; stride frequency
candidate_data: Published compilations of maximum and preferred locomotor speeds against body size for fish, birds and mammals, with body sizes from AnimalTraits or PanTHERIA.

label: Doubling gravity would make terrestrial animals short-legged or serpent-like
measurable_quantities: limb proportions; posture; skeletal and cardiovascular measures under altered gravity
candidate_data: Published hypergravity centrifuge and spaceflight studies of animal morphology and physiology.

label: Folded surfaces such as villi and brain convolutions keep surface in step with mass
measurable_quantities: intestinal absorptive surface area; cortical surface area or gyrification index; body or brain mass
candidate_data: Published comparative datasets of brain gyrification and cortical surface area across mammals and of intestinal surface area against body mass.

label: Form of small organisms is set by surface tension, not gravity, favouring spheres
measurable_quantities: organism size; shape sphericity or other shape descriptors; surface tension of cell boundaries
candidate_data: Plankton and protist imaging datasets with size and shape measurements, and cell-shape data in the Image Data Resource.

label: Form follows growth rates in large organisms but not in minute ones
measurable_quantities: directional growth rates; final shape; organism or cell size
candidate_data: Time-lapse growth and morphometric datasets of developing organisms and of single cells (Image Data Resource).

label: Cell division restores the ratio of surface to mass
measurable_quantities: cell volume; cell surface area; embryo total volume during cleavage
candidate_data: Cell-size and cell-cycle imaging datasets (Allen Cell Explorer, Image Data Resource) and published embryo cleavage volume measurements.

label: Cells of each kind vary little about a mean size, whatever the body size
measurable_quantities: cell size by tissue type; body size; cell number
candidate_data: Published cell-size measurements across body sizes within and between species, and tissue histology images in the Image Data Resource.

label: Ganglion-cell size varies little; larger species have ganglia with more cells
measurable_quantities: neuron soma size; neuron number per ganglion or brain region; body size
candidate_data: Published comparative neuron-count datasets (isotropic fractionator studies across mammals and birds) and NeuroMorpho.Org neuron morphologies.

label: The smallest organisms approach molecular size, so they cannot be much smaller
measurable_quantities: cell diameter of smallest organisms; number of protein molecules per cell
candidate_data: Published cell-size measurements of the smallest bacteria and archaea, and proteomic estimates of protein copy number per cell.

section: Form as a function of growth rates
label: External form results from the ratio of growth rates in different directions
measurable_quantities: directional growth rates (length, breadth, depth per unit time); shape descriptors over ontogeny
candidate_data: Longitudinal morphometric growth series and 3D developmental image time-lapses (e.g. published ontogenetic shape datasets on Dryad, MorphoSource specimen series).

section: Form as a function of growth rates
label: Constant growth-rate ratios preserve form; changing ratios produce development
measurable_quantities: ratios of linear dimensions over age; rate of change of shape indices
candidate_data: Longitudinal growth and shape datasets for animals and plants (e.g. ontogenetic morphometric series on Dryad, human growth cohort data).

label: Embryonic folds arise from local differences in growth rate of a uniform sheet
measurable_quantities: local tissue growth rates (cell proliferation, area expansion); fold geometry and timing
candidate_data: Live-imaging and cell-tracking datasets of chick and other vertebrate embryos during neurulation (e.g. Image Data Resource entries, published tissue-growth maps).

label: Differences between related forms emerge gradually and are small in the young
measurable_quantities: size and shape divergence between species across developmental stages; foetal body size by gestational age across species
candidate_data: Comparative embryo and foetal growth series and ontogenetic morphometric datasets (e.g. MorphoSource embryo scans, published comparative prenatal growth data).

label: Human stature grows fast in infancy, steadily in childhood, then quickens in the teens
measurable_quantities: stature by age; annual height increment by age
candidate_data: WHO and CDC growth reference data and national longitudinal growth cohort datasets.

label: Adult human stature declines well before fifty and markedly by old age
measurable_quantities: stature by age in adults; longitudinal height loss
candidate_data: Longitudinal ageing cohorts with repeated height measurement (e.g. Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging, NHANES cross-sectional data).

label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
measurable_quantities: body mass by age; stature by age
candidate_data: WHO/CDC growth references and longitudinal cohort data giving paired height and weight by age.

label: Boys and girls share a growth-velocity curve differing mainly in phase
measurable_quantities: annual weight and height increments by age and sex; age at peak growth velocity
candidate_data: Sex-specific growth velocity references (WHO, CDC) and longitudinal cohort datasets.

label: All animals pass through the same phases of growth: slow start, early peak, slowdown
measurable_quantities: body size by age; growth velocity by age; age at maximum growth velocity
candidate_data: Comparative growth-curve compilations (e.g. AnAge, published vertebrate growth-curve datasets on Dryad).

label: Cold-blooded animals approach a maximal size only asymptotically
measurable_quantities: length or mass at age; growth rate in late life
candidate_data: Fish length-at-age and growth-parameter compilations (e.g. FishBase growth data) and reptile growth records in AnAge.

label: Adult size results from both the rate and the duration of growth
measurable_quantities: adult body mass; growth rate; age at cessation of growth or maturity
candidate_data: Species-level life-history and growth databases (AnAge, PanTHERIA, AnimalTraits).

label: Human length growth peaks in velocity around the fifth month before birth
measurable_quantities: foetal length by gestational age; foetal length increment per month
candidate_data: Foetal growth standards from ultrasound studies (e.g. INTERGROWTH-21st foetal growth data, WHO foetal growth charts).

label: Variability of stature and weight tracks the rate of growth
measurable_quantities: coefficient of variation of stature and weight by age; mean growth velocity by age
candidate_data: Growth reference datasets reporting age-specific standard deviations (WHO, CDC, national growth surveys).

label: Growth rate is interrupted at physiological epochs such as birth, puberty, metamorphosis
measurable_quantities: growth velocity around birth, weaning, puberty, moults and metamorphosis
candidate_data: Longitudinal growth records of laboratory animals and insects (e.g. published mouse growth curves from the Mouse Phenome Database, insect larval growth datasets on Dryad).

label: Metamorphosis is often, perhaps always, accompanied by loss of bulk and weight
measurable_quantities: body mass and dimensions before and after metamorphosis
candidate_data: Published larval-to-juvenile body-size datasets for amphibians, insects and anguillid eels (e.g. Dryad metamorphosis size datasets).

label: Organ size bears no constant ratio to body size through life, especially the brain
measurable_quantities: organ weights by age; body weight by age
candidate_data: Autopsy organ-weight reference datasets by age and comparative ontogenetic organ-mass data.

label: Plaice weight-length coefficient peaks near the size of sexual maturity
measurable_quantities: fish length; fish weight; length at sexual maturity
candidate_data: Fisheries survey length-weight records and maturity data (e.g. ICES DATRAS survey data, FishBase length-weight relationships).

label: Seasonal cycle in fish weight at fixed length is caused by spawning
measurable_quantities: weight at fixed length by month; gonadosomatic index; spawning dates
candidate_data: Monthly fisheries sampling of length, weight and maturity stage (e.g. ICES survey and market-sampling data).

section: Form as a function of growth rates
label: Each part has its own specific growth rate, on which specific morphology depends
measurable_quantities: organ-specific growth rates; body proportions across species and ontogeny
candidate_data: Ontogenetic organ and limb growth datasets and comparative morphometrics (e.g. MorphoSource, Phenoscape, published relative-growth data on Dryad).

label: Common temperate plants share a growth optimum near 26 °C
measurable_quantities: growth rate versus temperature; optimal growth temperature by species
candidate_data: Plant thermal response compilations and TRY plant traits database entries on temperature optima.

label: Growth has a van’t Hoff temperature coefficient like a chemical reaction
measurable_quantities: growth or development rate at different temperatures; Q10
candidate_data: Compilations of thermal performance and development-rate data for ectotherms and plants (e.g. published Q10 and thermal performance curve datasets on Dryad).

label: Optimum temperature curves arise from acceleration combined with cumulative damage
measurable_quantities: growth rate versus temperature; growth rate versus exposure duration at high temperature
candidate_data: Thermal performance curve datasets with time-dependent exposure for plants and ectotherms (e.g. published thermal tolerance datasets on Dryad).

label: Seasonal growth in fish and man follows a damped sine curve
measurable_quantities: seasonal growth increments by age; amplitude of winter-summer growth difference
candidate_data: Fish otolith and scale increment datasets and human seasonal growth studies with sub-annual measurement.

label: Arizona tree rings show a regular 150-year climate periodicity
measurable_quantities: annual ring widths; spectral periodicity of ring-width series
candidate_data: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (ITRDB) ponderosa pine chronologies from Arizona and Southwest drought reconstructions (e.g. North American Drought Atlas).

label: Growth rate depends largely on water uptake (turgor) as well as metabolism
measurable_quantities: water uptake; turgor pressure; growth rate; dry mass change during growth
candidate_data: Plant cell expansion and turgor measurement studies and embryo water-content time series (published datasets on Dryad).

label: Brine-shrimp abdomen grows relatively longer the saltier the water
measurable_quantities: abdomen length / cephalothorax length ratio; water salinity or density
candidate_data: Artemia morphometric studies across salinity gradients and rearing experiments (published datasets on Dryad).

label: The organic curve of growth resembles the velocity curve of chemical autocatalysis
measurable_quantities: body size versus time; growth velocity versus time
candidate_data: Growth-curve datasets fitted with logistic and related models (e.g. published animal and plant growth curves on Dryad, AnAge).

label: Internal secretions and other substances accelerate growth and alter proportions
measurable_quantities: growth rates of specific organs under hormone treatment; body proportions
candidate_data: Experimental endocrinology datasets on thyroid hormone in amphibian metamorphosis and growth hormone effects on body proportions (published studies on Dryad).

label: Natural selection removes forms rather than originating them
candidate_data: none known

label: Velocity of regenerative growth varies inversely as about the square of time
measurable_quantities: regenerated length versus days after amputation; daily regeneration increment
candidate_data: Time-course regeneration measurements in amphibian larvae and zebrafish fins (published datasets on Dryad).

label: Regeneration is ordinary growth, with the same curve as growth from zero
measurable_quantities: regeneration velocity versus time; embryonic growth velocity versus time from conception
candidate_data: Regeneration time-course data (amphibians, zebrafish) alongside prenatal growth curves (published datasets on Dryad).

label: Claw reversal after amputation depends on regeneration versus growth rates
measurable_quantities: growth rate of regenerating claw; growth rate of intact claw; claw size and form over successive moults
candidate_data: Snapping shrimp and crab claw-regeneration experiment data (published studies on Dryad).

label: Reproduction by fission is a physical tendency to segment plus regeneration
measurable_quantities: body length at fission; body rigidity; phylogenetic distribution of fission
candidate_data: Phylogenetic trait data on asexual fission in annelids and flatworms combined with body-size data (e.g. published comparative datasets).

label: Growth velocity peaks and falls because surface resistance suddenly increases
measurable_quantities: timing of peak growth velocity; timing of skin or tissue differentiation; tissue stiffness
candidate_data: Developmental tissue-mechanics measurements paired with growth time series (published embryo mechanics datasets).

label: Form changes follow the same route in individual development and racial history
measurable_quantities: ontogenetic shape trajectories; phylogenetic shape trajectories
candidate_data: Geometric morphometric datasets with ontogenetic and phylogenetic series (e.g. MorphoSource, Paleobiology Database occurrence and size data).

label: Cell structure matters only as the visible expression of forces and energy
candidate_data: none known

section: Spindle and asters as lines of force
label: Mitotic figures require a polarised force like magnetism, not mechanical traction
measurable_quantities: spindle and aster fibre geometry; forces on chromosomes and spindle poles; intracellular electric fields during mitosis
candidate_data: Published spindle mechanics and microtubule imaging studies (Image Data Resource mitotic screens such as MitoCheck) bear on the mechanism.

label: The nucleus is spherical because it is an immiscible fluid drop under uniform tension
measurable_quantities: nuclear sphericity or aspect ratio; cytoplasmic stiffness or viscosity; nuclear surface tension
candidate_data: Single-cell 3D imaging with segmented nuclear shapes (Allen Cell Explorer, Image Data Resource) combined with published cytoplasmic and nuclear mechanics measurements.

label: Morphological polarity of the cell is the outward sign of a dynamical polarity
measurable_quantities: orientation of granule or fibril alignment; cell axis orientation; intracellular force or field distribution
candidate_data: Imaging datasets of polarised epithelial cells (Image Data Resource) and published intracellular force or electric-field measurements.

label: The alveolar meshwork of nucleus and cytoplasm is a surface-tension froth
measurable_quantities: alveolus size distribution; interfacial tension between cytoplasmic phases; density of intermixed fluid phases
candidate_data: Live-cell and electron-microscopy image collections (Image Data Resource, EMPIAR) and published measurements of cytoplasmic phase separation.

label: Fine internal networks and granules seen in fixed cells are largely artefacts
measurable_quantities: presence and morphology of intracellular networks in living versus fixed cells; variation of fixed structure with fixative used
candidate_data: Paired live-cell and fixed-cell imaging studies and cryo-electron tomography datasets (EMPIAR) comparing preserved structure.

section: Nucleus and chromatin in the field
label: Chromatin behaves as a diamagnetic body and moves to the equatorial plane
measurable_quantities: chromosome position relative to spindle poles over time; chromosome distribution on the metaphase plate; field strength along the spindle
candidate_data: Live-cell time-lapse mitosis imaging datasets (Image Data Resource, Cell Tracking Challenge) give chromosome trajectories.

label: Differences of electric potential play a great part in cell division
measurable_quantities: transcellular or animal–vegetal potential difference; timing of potential reversals relative to cleavage; electrophoretic mobility of nuclei and cytoplasm
candidate_data: Published bioelectric measurements in eggs and embryos (vibrating-probe and voltage-dye studies) deposited in supplementary data or Dryad.

label: Every cell division results from conflict between surface tension and opposing forces
measurable_quantities: cortical tension at equator and poles during cytokinesis; internal pressure; orientation of cleavage plane relative to spindle axis
candidate_data: Published micropipette aspiration and cortical tension measurements during cytokinesis, and mitosis imaging datasets in the Image Data Resource.

label: Entry of the first spermatozoon raises the surface tension of the egg
measurable_quantities: egg surface tension or cortical tension before and after sperm entry; rate of supernumerary sperm entry
candidate_data: Published measurements of egg cortical stiffness and polyspermy block in sea urchin, frog and mouse eggs.

label: The pronuclei travel curved paths and meet before reaching the centre of the egg
measurable_quantities: 3D trajectories of male and female pronuclei; position of pronuclear meeting relative to egg centre
candidate_data: Live 3D time-lapse imaging of pronuclear migration in sea urchin, C. elegans or mouse zygotes (Image Data Resource and published supplementary data).

label: Mitotic phenomena follow from simple physical assumptions and have secondary significance
candidate_data: none known

label: Chromosome numbers of germ-nuclei mostly lie between six and sixteen
measurable_quantities: haploid chromosome number across species
candidate_data: Chromosome Counts Database (CCDB) for plants and published animal karyotype compilations.

label: Details of mitosis vary among close relatives and are not specific to the organism
measurable_quantities: mitotic mode (open or closed, centrosomal or acentrosomal); chromosome morphology; phylogenetic signal of mitotic traits
candidate_data: Comparative cytology compilations of mitotic types across eukaryotes combined with phylogenies from the Open Tree of Life.

label: Early embryological categories seldom coincide with phylogenetic classification
measurable_quantities: egg yolk content; cleavage type; chromosome number and form; phylogenetic signal of these traits
candidate_data: Comparative datasets of egg size and cleavage type mapped onto animal phylogenies (Open Tree of Life; published egg-size compilations on Dryad).

section: The cell as a sphere of action
label: Surface tension gives the cell its outline and morphological individuality
measurable_quantities: interfacial tension at cell boundaries; completeness of cleavage furrows; cell shape
candidate_data: Published measurements of cortical and interfacial tension in embryos combined with embryo imaging datasets.

label: The centrosome is essentially a centre of force, not necessarily a material body
measurable_quantities: presence or absence of centrosomes; de novo centrosome formation; spindle pole organisation without centrosomes
candidate_data: Published studies of acentrosomal spindles and de novo centriole formation, and cell imaging datasets (Allen Cell Explorer).

label: A continuous field of force shapes the whole organism regardless of its cells
measurable_quantities: organ shape versus cell number and cell size; effect of altered cell size or number on organ form
candidate_data: Published experiments on polyploid or cell-number-altered organisms (e.g. plant leaf and Drosophila wing size studies) with organ morphometrics.

section: Growth by imbibition versus crystal growth
label: Fluid protoplasm growing by imbibition produces rounded rather than plane surfaces
measurable_quantities: proportion of curved versus planar surface in cell and organism outlines; surface curvature distribution
candidate_data: 3D cell segmentation and shape datasets such as the Allen Cell Explorer and Image Data Resource, compared with crystal morphology databases.

section: Surface tension and the forms of cells
label: Surface tension is probably the paramount force determining cell form
measurable_quantities: cortical or membrane tension; cell shape descriptors; internal pressure; external mechanical loads
candidate_data: Published micropipette aspiration and AFM measurements of cortical tension paired with cell shape imaging, e.g. Allen Cell Explorer and Image Data Resource datasets.

label: Organic symmetry reflects equilibrium and is absent without it, as in amoeba
measurable_quantities: degree of shape symmetry; shape fluctuation over time (stability)
candidate_data: Time-lapse cell shape datasets (e.g. Image Data Resource, Cell Image Library) allowing comparison of symmetry measures between motile and resting cells.

section: Surface tension in protoplasm and amoeba
label: Rounding off of protoplasm is due to surface tension, not vital contractility
measurable_quantities: rounding kinetics of protoplasm; surface or cortical tension; effect of inhibiting active contractile machinery on rounding
candidate_data: Published cell-rounding and cortical tension measurements with and without myosin inhibition; live-imaging datasets in the Image Data Resource.

section: Surface tension in protoplasm and amoeba
label: Plasmodial taxes towards moisture, warmth and food parallel surface-tension phenomena
measurable_quantities: direction and speed of migration in gradients; local surface tension of the plasmodium; temperature, humidity and solute gradients
candidate_data: Published Physarum chemotaxis and thermotaxis assays and tension/rheology measurements; none known as a central database.

section: Surface tension in protoplasm and amoeba
label: Resting cells are spherical; the amoeboid phase is one of activity and unequal tensions
measurable_quantities: cell sphericity; metabolic or motile activity; presence of cyst wall
candidate_data: Imaging and encystment studies of Acanthamoeba and other amoebae; Image Data Resource time-lapse datasets.

section: Budding yeast and localised tension changes
label: A yeast bud arises where surface tension locally and suddenly diminishes
measurable_quantities: local cell-wall or membrane tension and extensibility at the bud site; bud shape over time
candidate_data: Yeast cell-wall mechanics (AFM) and bud morphology imaging, e.g. SCMD (Saccharomyces cerevisiae Morphological Database).

label: Each new foraminiferal chamber is a surface-tension figure; the whole shell is not
measurable_quantities: shape of individual chambers (closeness to constant-mean-curvature surfaces); chamber contact angles
candidate_data: Micro-CT foraminiferal shell scans in MorphoSource and published 3D chamber reconstructions; Endless Forams image collection.

label: Surface tension governs the forms of small organisms and cells, not large organisms
measurable_quantities: body or cell size; specific surface (surface-to-volume ratio); agreement of shape with surface-tension figures
candidate_data: Cell and organism size and shape compilations (e.g. Allen Cell Explorer for cells, AnimalTraits for body size) combined with shape measurements.

section: Plateau's surfaces of revolution in cells
label: Spheres, cylinders and unduloids are the commonest unicellular forms
measurable_quantities: frequency of cell shape classes; fit of cell outlines to sphere, cylinder and unduloid profiles
candidate_data: Protist and bacterial image collections (e.g. EcoTaxa plankton images, Image Data Resource, Cell Image Library) analysed for shape classes.

label: A cylindrical cell's end cap has twice the cylinder's radius and height about 0.27R
measurable_quantities: cylinder radius; end-cap radius of curvature; end-cap height
candidate_data: Micrographs of filamentous algae and of rod-shaped bacteria pole geometry from published imaging datasets (e.g. Image Data Resource).

section: Instability of liquid cylinders and beading
label: Viscid spider-thread coating breaks into beads at the cylinder stability limit
measurable_quantities: coating thickness or radius; bead spacing; bead size; presence of satellite beads
candidate_data: Published measurements of glue droplet spacing and size on orb-web capture threads (including datasets deposited on Dryad).

label: Notched hydroid cups and annulated stems are both due to surface tension
measurable_quantities: number and spacing of rim teeth relative to rim circumference; annulation spacing relative to stem diameter
candidate_data: Hydroid specimen images in museum collections and GBIF-linked media, with morphometric measurement.

label: Freely growing cylindrical cells owe their form to an anisotropic wall
measurable_quantities: wall anisotropy (e.g. microfibril orientation); directional wall extensibility; cell aspect ratio
candidate_data: Published cellulose microfibril orientation and wall mechanics data for algal and plant cells; Plant Cell Atlas imaging resources.

section: Limited range of forms in small organisms
label: Small organisms show a limited range of forms because molecular forces control them
measurable_quantities: morphological disparity (shape diversity) versus organism size
candidate_data: Large plankton and microbial image sets (e.g. EcoTaxa) and bacterial shape compilations compared with metazoan morphospace data from Phenoscape or MorphoSource.

section: Limited range of forms in small organisms
label: Bacterial form is too plastic to serve for species identification
measurable_quantities: within-species shape variation across conditions; between-species shape differences
candidate_data: Bacterial cell morphology imaging datasets across growth conditions (e.g. published Dryad and Image Data Resource collections) paired with species identity.

label: Vorticella bells form a graded series of unduloids
measurable_quantities: bell outline profile; fit to unduloid (Delaunay surface) meridian; ratio of neck to bulge radius
candidate_data: Ciliate micrograph collections (e.g. EcoTaxa, published Vorticella morphometric studies) for outline fitting.

label: Protozoan loricas form by adsorption into least-area surfaces, not for protection
measurable_quantities: lorica outline profile; fit to constant-mean-curvature surfaces
candidate_data: Tintinnid lorica morphometric datasets and plankton imaging collections such as EcoTaxa.

label: Shared form in simple organisms need not imply common descent
measurable_quantities: morphological similarity; molecular phylogenetic relatedness; frequency of morphological convergence
candidate_data: Molecular phylogenies of foraminifera and ciliates (e.g. PR2 ribosomal database, GenBank sequences) compared with morphospecies assignments and fossil occurrences in the Paleobiology Database.

section: Foraminiferal shells and position of symmetry
label: The unduloid Lagena shell is formed while hanging vertically in the sea
measurable_quantities: orientation of living organism during shell formation; shell axial symmetry; presence of lateral flattening or wings
candidate_data: Field and culture observations of Lagena life position and shell morphometrics from foraminiferal collections; none known as a database.

label: Thin walls flute longitudinally; thick narrow necks pleat transversely
measurable_quantities: orientation of folds; wall thickness to diameter ratio; local curvature
candidate_data: Foraminiferal shell images and micro-CT in MorphoSource and museum collections, measured for fold orientation and wall thickness.

label: Symmetrical surface-tension pull sets heliozoan filaments radially
measurable_quantities: angle of axopodia to cell surface; contact-angle profile of protoplasm on filaments
candidate_data: Published imaging of heliozoan axopodia; no dedicated database known.

label: The trypanosome undulating membrane is a liquid film drawn up along a flagellum
measurable_quantities: membrane shape and curvature; development sequence of the membrane; flagellum attachment
candidate_data: Electron microscopy and live imaging of trypanosome and Trichomonas morphology, e.g. the TrypTag localisation resource and the Image Data Resource.

label: The biconcave red blood corpuscle is not a surface-tension equilibrium figure
measurable_quantities: red cell surface curvature profile; cell shape versus medium tonicity; membrane elastic properties
candidate_data: Published erythrocyte shape and osmotic fragility datasets and red cell membrane mechanics measurements.

label: Decapod sperm-cell shape is an intermediate phase of osmotic shrinkage
measurable_quantities: cell shape as a function of external osmolarity; cell volume; surface area
candidate_data: Published osmotic-response studies of decapod spermatozoa; no dedicated database known.

label: Elastic fibrillae act as a microscopic skeleton shaping spiral cells
measurable_quantities: presence and arrangement of cortical fibrillar structures; change of shape when fibrils are disrupted
candidate_data: Electron microscopy and cytoskeleton imaging of ciliates and sperm cells, e.g. the Cell Image Library and EMPIAR.

label: Cell-wall secretion is adsorption of constituents at the surface
measurable_quantities: surface activity of wall precursors; surface concentration of wall materials during wall formation
candidate_data: Biochemical and imaging studies of cell-wall deposition; no single database known.

label: Spicules are deposited at interfaces between cells or vacuoles
measurable_quantities: location of spicule deposition relative to cell and vacuole boundaries; correspondence of spicule geometry with boundary geometry
candidate_data: Electron microscopy of sponge sclerocytes and radiolarian skeletogenesis (e.g. EMPIAR, Cell Image Library) and radiolarian image collections.

label: Membranes and cysts form only after protoplasm rounds up with positive surface tension
measurable_quantities: timing of cyst-wall deposition relative to cell rounding; cell surface tension
candidate_data: Time-lapse encystment studies of Acanthamoeba, Entamoeba or Physarum; Image Data Resource time-lapse datasets.

label: Winter encystment and winter-egg shells relate to temperature effects on adsorption
measurable_quantities: encystment rate versus temperature; egg shell thickness versus temperature or season
candidate_data: Published Daphnia ephippia and rotifer resting-egg induction experiments and protist encystment-temperature studies (e.g. Dryad datasets).

label: Chondriosomes and similar fibrils are surface-tension clumps drawn along the cell axis
measurable_quantities: orientation of mitochondria relative to cell axis; dependence of their arrangement on cytoplasmic flows
candidate_data: Mitochondrial imaging in the Allen Cell Explorer and Human Protein Atlas subcellular atlas, with studies of cytoplasmic streaming.

label: Potassium salts concentrate where cell-surface tension is weak
measurable_quantities: local potassium concentration at cell surfaces; local surface or wall tension
candidate_data: Potassium-sensitive fluorescent indicator imaging and X-ray microanalysis studies of cells; no dedicated database known.

label: Conjugation outgrowths and root-hairs arise at sites of potassium concentration
measurable_quantities: potassium concentration at outgrowth sites versus elsewhere; timing of potassium accumulation relative to bulging
candidate_data: Ion imaging studies of tip growth in root hairs and pollen tubes and of algal conjugation; no dedicated database known.

label: Potassium accumulates at the bases of cilia and flagella
measurable_quantities: potassium concentration near ciliary bases; local surface protrusion at flagellar base
candidate_data: Ion imaging and elemental microanalysis of ciliated cells; ciliary proteomics resources such as CiliaCarta do not directly address ions.

label: Unicellular forms and their asymmetries follow surface molecular forces
measurable_quantities: cell shape and asymmetry; spatial distribution of surface tension or cortical tension
candidate_data: Combined cell-shape imaging (Allen Cell Explorer, Image Data Resource) and cortical tension mapping studies.

label: Forms of cell-aggregates are shaped chiefly by surface tension toward minimal areas
measurable_quantities: cell-wall junction angles; cell-wall curvature; interfacial tensions; total interface area relative to minimal configurations
candidate_data: Segmented 2D and 3D tissue images (e.g. Image Data Resource, Allen Cell Explorer) combined with published cortical-tension and laser-ablation measurements of cell interfaces.

section: Three surfaces in contact and Sachs’s Rule
label: Right-angled cell walls arise because older walls solidify before new partitions form
measurable_quantities: angle at which new partitions meet existing walls; rigidity of parent wall at time of division
candidate_data: Time-lapse confocal imaging of plant meristems and segmented plant tissue datasets (e.g. published Arabidopsis shoot-apex segmentations on public repositories) giving junction angles of new versus old walls.

label: Shape of paired cells depends on relative tensions at outer surface and partition
measurable_quantities: contact angle between adjacent cells; partition diameter relative to cell diameter; ratio of cell–cell to cell–medium surface tension
candidate_data: Published micropipette and contact-angle measurements of cell doublets, and microscopy images of cyanobacterial filaments from public image collections.

label: Tissue cell walls meet three at a time at 120°, regardless of cell size
measurable_quantities: number of walls meeting at each vertex; angles between walls at vertices; wall curvature versus size difference of neighbouring cells
candidate_data: Segmented epithelial and plant tissue images (e.g. Image Data Resource, published Drosophila wing-disc and plant meristem segmentations) from which vertex degree and junction angles can be measured.

label: Four cells of a segmenting egg never meet in a point; a polar furrow is always present
measurable_quantities: presence and length of polar (cross) furrow; number of cells meeting at the animal and vegetal poles
candidate_data: Live-imaging and 3D segmentation datasets of early cleavage-stage embryos (e.g. published ascidian, sea urchin and frog embryo atlases) in which pole junction topology can be scored.

section: Unequal tensions and rounding of blastomeres
label: Strong cell–cell tension relative to cell–medium tension makes cells round off
measurable_quantities: external contact angle between cells; cell–cell and cell–medium interfacial tensions; contact area between cells
candidate_data: Published measurements of blastomere contact angles and cortical tension (micropipette aspiration) in early embryos, e.g. mouse and ascidian compaction studies.

section: Epidermal layer as a positional effect
label: An epidermis’s physical characters follow simply from its lying on the outside
measurable_quantities: shape and aspect ratio of outer versus inner cells; angles at which anticlinal walls meet the outer wall; outer wall thickness
candidate_data: Segmented plant tissue sections and confocal stacks in public image repositories (e.g. Image Data Resource) comparing outer-layer and inner-layer cell geometry.

label: Hexagons are regular only where cells are equal in size and forces uniform
measurable_quantities: coefficient of variation of cell area; fraction of hexagonal cells; cell elongation
candidate_data: Published retinal pigment epithelium flat-mount morphometry datasets and segmented intestinal epithelium images in public repositories such as Image Data Resource.

label: Cylinders or spheres pressed into full surface contact form hexagons
measurable_quantities: number of sides per cell; frequency of hexagons; vertex angles
candidate_data: Segmented epithelial images (e.g. Image Data Resource) giving polygon-number distributions, and coral specimen images in MorphoSource.

label: Close-packed corallites of varying size are on average hexagonal
measurable_quantities: number of sides per corallite; corallite size variance; colony growth form (massive or fasciculate)
candidate_data: Coral specimen images and 3D scans in MorphoSource and fossil occurrence and growth-form data in the Paleobiology Database.

label: The bee’s cell is a hexagonal prism capped by rhombic-dodecahedral facets
measurable_quantities: rhomb angles at the base of the cell; cell wall angles; wax surface area per unit cell volume
candidate_data: Published micro-CT studies of honeybee comb geometry and 3D scans of combs; no single standard repository known.

label: Comb geometry arises from surface tension in semi-fluid wax, not bee design
measurable_quantities: wax temperature during building; cell shape at initial construction versus later; wall angle changes over time
candidate_data: Published thermography and time-lapse studies of honeybee comb construction; no dedicated public database known.

label: Parenchyma cells are generally rhombic dodecahedra, ideal froths tetrakaidecahedra
measurable_quantities: number of faces per cell; number of quadrilateral, pentagonal and hexagonal faces
candidate_data: 3D segmented plant tissue volumes from confocal or micro-CT imaging in public repositories (e.g. Image Data Resource), giving face counts per cell.

label: Physical laws govern the whole configuration of later-stage segmenting eggs
measurable_quantities: cell positions and shapes in embryos; agreement of physical foam or vertex models with observed embryo geometry
candidate_data: Published 3D cell-shape atlases of early embryos (e.g. C. elegans and ascidian embryo segmentations) compared against foam and vertex-model simulations.

section: Polar furrow variants and cell size
label: Polar-furrow arrangements follow relative cell sizes, not species identity
measurable_quantities: upper and lower polar furrow lengths; relative blastomere volumes; taxon of embryo
candidate_data: Published blastomere volume and cleavage-geometry measurements from imaging studies of early spiralian, ascidian and frog embryos.

label: No evidence that physical forces give way to unknown vital agencies in development
candidate_data: none known

label: Minimal bisecting walls cut the longest axis and alternate at right angles
measurable_quantities: orientation of division plane relative to cell long axis; angle between successive division planes
candidate_data: Time-lapse lineage-tracked plant meristem and early embryo datasets (e.g. published Arabidopsis embryo and shoot-apex segmentations) recording division-plane orientation.

section: Sachs’s and Errera’s rules of division
label: A new cell wall has the least area that can enclose the given volume (Errera)
measurable_quantities: area of new partition; area of alternative partitions dividing the same volume; cell shape before division
candidate_data: Published 3D segmented plant embryo and meristem datasets in which observed division planes have been compared to computed minimal-area planes.

section: Unequal division of a cubical cell
label: A cell cutting off under ~3/10 of its volume uses a curved corner wall, not a plane
measurable_quantities: volume fraction cut off; partition shape (plane, cylindrical or spherical); partition area
candidate_data: Imaging datasets of asymmetric divisions in plant epidermis (e.g. published stomatal lineage time-lapse studies) giving daughter volume ratios and wall shapes.

section: Division of a flattened quadrant cell
label: A quadrant-shaped flat cell divides by a curved anticlinal wall about 3:7 along its side
measurable_quantities: position of new wall on the radial side; arc angle cut off; shape of new wall
candidate_data: Imaging of compressed early embryos and discoid algal thalli in published developmental studies; no dedicated database known.

label: Sector cells divide anticlinally only between 62½° and 90°, otherwise periclinally
measurable_quantities: sector angle of the mother cell; orientation of the new partition (anticlinal or periclinal)
candidate_data: Lineage-tracked plant embryo and meristem segmentations (published Arabidopsis embryo atlases) in which mother-cell geometry and division orientation can be scored.

section: Uniform growth and unequal cell division
label: Uniform growth of a disc makes its daughter cells divide at different times
measurable_quantities: timing of division of sister cells; cell area growth rate by position; disc radius at division
candidate_data: Time-lapse imaging of discoid algal or plant tissue growth with lineage tracking; no dedicated public dataset known.

section: Origin of an epidermis by minimal-area division
label: Successive minimal-area divisions leave quadrilateral cells forming an epidermis
measurable_quantities: shape of peripheral versus interior cells; orientation of divisions in the outer layer
candidate_data: Published segmented plant embryo atlases (e.g. Arabidopsis early embryo 3D segmentations) giving protoderm formation and division orientations.

label: The arrangement of the first eight cells is not a constant character of a species
measurable_quantities: frequency of each eight-cell arrangement type within a species
candidate_data: Large samples of imaged Xenopus or other amphibian eight-cell embryos from published developmental imaging studies; Xenbase may hold relevant images.

label: All surface groupings of eight cells belong to one of thirteen types
measurable_quantities: topological arrangement of cell junctions; number of intermediate partitions
candidate_data: Segmented images of eight-cell embryos and plant tissues from published embryo atlases, scored for junction topology.

label: Most stable cell groupings spread contacts evenly; unstable ones concentrate them
measurable_quantities: number of contacts per cell; frequency of each arrangement type; persistence time of arrangements
candidate_data: Live-imaging datasets of early cleavage embryos and foam or emulsion experiments recording neighbour topology over time.

label: Few partition patterns recur across organisms regardless of classification
measurable_quantities: frequency of each partition topology by taxon; phylogenetic signal of partition topology
candidate_data: Cleavage-pattern descriptions compiled across taxa from published embryological imaging, combined with phylogenies (e.g. Open Tree of Life) to test phylogenetic signal.

label: A coral fossula reflects space-partitioning, not higher bilateral organisation
measurable_quantities: septal junction topology; presence of fossulae; phylogenetic position of taxa
candidate_data: Fossil coral specimen images in MorphoSource and occurrence and taxonomy data in the Paleobiology Database.

label: Stomata lie in rows on oblong-celled leaves and scattered on polygonal-celled ones
measurable_quantities: epidermal cell aspect ratio; spatial arrangement of stomata (row alignment index)
candidate_data: Leaf epidermis micrograph collections and stomatal trait datasets (e.g. TRY plant traits for stomatal density, published leaf-epidermis image datasets).

label: Pollen-grain shape depends on whether walls harden before the tetrad separates
measurable_quantities: timing of wall hardening relative to tetrad separation; facet angularity of mature grains
candidate_data: Palynological image databases (e.g. PalDat) of pollen morphology combined with developmental studies of tetrad separation timing.

label: Outgrowths tend to arise from triangular rather than quadrangular cells
measurable_quantities: shape of cells giving rise to buds; frequency of bud initiation by cell shape
candidate_data: Published lineage studies of bud and branch initiation in moss protonemata and fern gametophytes; no dedicated database known.

section: Growth rate and plane of division
label: Division plane depends on the ratio of growth rate to division frequency
measurable_quantities: cell length-to-width ratio before division; growth rate; division interval; division-plane orientation
candidate_data: Time-lapse imaging of moss protonemata and apical cells (e.g. published Physcomitrium growth studies) giving growth rates and division planes.

label: Cell division pattern is the result, not the cause, of the form of the growing mass
measurable_quantities: organ shape change over time; cell division orientation and rate; regional growth rates
candidate_data: Published time-lapse growth-tracking datasets of plant organs and mutants with altered cell division but normal shape (e.g. lineage-tracked shoot apex and leaf datasets).

label: Skeletal salts precipitate in dead or inactive matrix, not living protoplasm
measurable_quantities: location of mineral nucleation sites relative to cells; cell viability at mineralisation sites
candidate_data: Published electron-microscopy and correlative imaging studies of biomineralisation sites (e.g. matrix vesicles in cartilage, sponge sclerocytes), including image sets in the Image Data Resource or EMPIAR.

label: Sea-urchin larvae reared without lime develop healthily but lack skeletal rods and arms
measurable_quantities: calcium concentration of rearing water; larval spicule length; larval arm length; larval survival
candidate_data: Published sea-urchin larval culture experiments under low-calcium and ocean-acidification conditions, many with data deposited on Dryad or PANGAEA.

label: Biological molecular asymmetry may originate from circularly polarised sunlight
measurable_quantities: enantiomeric excess produced by circularly polarised light photolysis; circular polarisation of natural light
candidate_data: Laboratory photochemistry studies of enantiomeric excess under circularly polarised light, and enantiomeric analyses of amino acids in carbonaceous meteorites.

label: Pearls and bony-fish otoliths share the structure of artificial calcospherites
measurable_quantities: crystal fabric (radial/concentric) of concretions; mineral polymorph; organic content
candidate_data: Published microstructural (SEM, EBSD) studies of otoliths and pearls compared with biomimetic calcium carbonate precipitates in protein gels.

label: Concentric growth rings need not record periodic external conditions such as seasons
measurable_quantities: number of otolith or scale zones; known age of fish; seasonal temperature amplitude of habitat
candidate_data: Otolith age-validation studies using known-age or marked fish and bomb-radiocarbon dating, including deep-sea species; fisheries otolith archives.

section: Solubility of calcium salts in colloids
label: Calcium salts precipitate when the albumins holding them in solution break down
measurable_quantities: solubility of calcium salts in protein solutions vs. protein hydrolysates; protein degradation at mineralisation sites
candidate_data: Published physical-chemistry measurements of calcium phosphate and carbonate solubility in the presence of proteins and peptides, and studies of protease activity at mineralisation fronts.

section: Classification of skeletal forms by scale
label: Cell-sized skeletal elements are shaped by molecular forces, large ones by mechanics
candidate_data: none known

section: Spicules confined to a cell surface
label: A straight-growing spicule confined to a cell surface grows along a geodetic
measurable_quantities: 3D curvature and torsion of spicules; shape and axes of the sclerocyte; spicule orientation relative to cell axes
candidate_data: Micro-CT and SEM image sets of sponge spicules (e.g. in MorphoSource) and published sclerocyte imaging studies.

section: Spicules confined to a cell surface
label: Like spicules in silica and calcite show form is set by external forces, not chemistry
measurable_quantities: spicule shape descriptors in sponges and holothurians; spicule mineral composition
candidate_data: Comparative morphometric data from spicule image collections (e.g. MorphoSource, museum SEM archives) and the World Porifera Database for taxonomic context.

label: Triradiate spicules form at three-cell junctions with rays at 120°, four-rayed at ~109°
measurable_quantities: inter-ray angles of spicules; ray curvature; size and arrangement of surrounding cells or chambers
candidate_data: Micro-CT and SEM spicule images (e.g. MorphoSource) and published developmental imaging of calcareous sponge spicule formation by sclerocytes.

label: Six-rayed hexactinellid spicules reflect cubic, not closest, packing of vesicles
measurable_quantities: spatial arrangement of chambers or syncytial units around forming spicules; spicule ray orientations
candidate_data: Published histological and 3D imaging studies of hexactinellid tissue and spicule formation.

label: Radiolarian species lack definite geographic ranges and many co-occur locally
measurable_quantities: geographic range sizes of radiolarian species; species richness and dominance per sample; stratigraphic ranges of genera and families
candidate_data: Radiolarian occurrence data in GBIF, the Paleobiology Database and the Neptune microfossil database; plankton net and sediment-trap census counts.

label: Agglutinated protist shells form by surface energy, not choice or skill
measurable_quantities: particle types incorporated vs. available; particle wettability or surface energy; test construction time
candidate_data: Published experiments on testate amoeba and agglutinated foraminifera grain selection, and sediment-versus-test grain composition studies.

label: Hexagonal lattice shells form as silica collects in grooves between surface vesicles
measurable_quantities: mesh polygon size distribution and side number; size distribution of underlying alveoli/vesicles
candidate_data: SEM image collections of radiolarian shells and published live-cell imaging of radiolarian cytoplasm and skeletogenesis.

label: Lattice-shell form is independent of the material, being moulded on vesicles
measurable_quantities: mesh regularity of shells of different composition; skeletal composition
candidate_data: Comparative SEM images of siliceous radiolarians, acantharians and Clathrulina from museum and published collections.

label: Callimitra's skeleton is formed on the interfaces of a tetrahedral group of four cells
measurable_quantities: angles between skeletal plates and edges; cytoplasmic organisation during skeletogenesis
candidate_data: Micro-CT or SEM reconstructions of nassellarian skeletons and published studies of radiolarian skeletogenesis.

label: Regular dodecahedral radiolarian shells cannot arise by crystal-like space partitioning
measurable_quantities: vertex angles and face regularity of polyhedral shells; number and positions of radial spines
candidate_data: 3D reconstructions (micro-CT, SEM tilt series) of polyhedral radiolarian shells from museum collections.

label: Twenty-spined Radiolaria have hexagonal symmetry, not Müller's arrangement
measurable_quantities: angular positions (latitude and longitude) of the twenty spines
candidate_data: 3D imaging of acantharian skeletons and published spine-geometry measurements of Acantharia.

label: Radiolarian axial polarity arises in the central protoplasm, unexplained by mechanics
measurable_quantities: site of spine initiation relative to central capsule; spine arrangement in early developmental stages
candidate_data: Published developmental and cytological studies of acantharian spine formation.

label: Annular, longitudinal and spiral wall thickenings of plant cells are cylinder geodetics
measurable_quantities: orientation and pitch of wall thickenings; cell or tube diameter
candidate_data: Plant anatomy image collections and published micro-CT of xylem secondary walls and insect tracheae.

label: The suture of a turreted shell is a conical geodetic with coils closing toward the apex
measurable_quantities: suture path on the shell surface; whorl spacing versus shell diameter along the spire
candidate_data: 3D surface scans of gastropod shells in MorphoSource and museum collections.

label: Two crossing systems of geodetic spirals are a common source of reticulated patterns
measurable_quantities: angles and geodesic deviation of the crossing pattern lines on the surface
candidate_data: Image collections of reticulate cell-wall thickenings and other surface patterns; none specifically compiled.

label: Muscle fibres on hollow organs arrange themselves along geodesic curves
measurable_quantities: 3D muscle fibre orientations on organ surfaces; geodesic paths on the reconstructed organ surface
candidate_data: Diffusion-tensor MRI fibre-orientation atlases of the heart and gut, and published histological fibre-orientation maps.

label: Heart and stomach fibres stay geodetic after the twisting of the primitive tube
measurable_quantities: myocardial and gastric fibre orientations; deviation of fibre paths from surface geodesics; developmental fibre orientation in heart tube looping
candidate_data: Cardiac diffusion-tensor MRI datasets and developmental imaging of heart-tube looping in model organisms.

label: Small swimmers rotate about their axis, turning a constant swerve into a helical path
measurable_quantities: body rotation rate; helix radius and pitch of swimming trajectories; net displacement versus path length
candidate_data: Published 3D tracking datasets of microorganism swimming trajectories (e.g. on Dryad or Zenodo).

label: Horns, molluscan shells, foraminifera and sunflower florets follow the logarithmic spiral
measurable_quantities: polar radius as a function of vectorial angle; goodness of fit of logarithmic versus other spiral models
candidate_data: 3D surface scans and CT images of shells and horns from MorphoSource, and published sunflower capitulum images, fitted with spiral models.

label: A spiral needs a deflecting force carried by the growing body, not an external one
measurable_quantities: shell coiling direction relative to gravity; columellar muscle attachment and force; coiling in muscle-less shells
candidate_data: Studies of gastropod shell coiling under altered orientation or microgravity and anatomical data on columellar muscle; none known as a dedicated dataset.

label: A constant ratio of longitudinal to transverse growth rates yields a logarithmic spiral
measurable_quantities: growth rate at outer versus inner margin of the aperture; spiral constant angle
candidate_data: Sclerochronological growth-increment measurements on shells and horn growth-ring data, combined with spiral-angle measurements from CT scans (e.g. MorphoSource).

label: The scorpioid cyme traces a true logarithmic spiral
measurable_quantities: branching angle between successive shoots; ratio of successive shoot lengths
candidate_data: Herbarium specimen images (e.g. via GBIF) and plant architecture measurements of Boraginaceae inflorescences.

label: The shell grows in size without changing its shape
measurable_quantities: shape descriptors of juvenile versus adult shells; spiral parameters measured at different growth stages
candidate_data: Ontogenetic series of shell CT scans or images (MorphoSource, museum collections) analysed with geometric morphometrics.

label: Each increment of a spirally grown structure is a gnomon to the whole before it
measurable_quantities: shape of successive growth increments or chambers; similarity of whole structure before and after each increment
candidate_data: Micro-CT chamber-by-chamber reconstructions of foraminifera and cephalopod shells (e.g. MorphoSource) and horn growth-ring images.

label: Logarithmic spirals occur in accreted hard parts, not in simultaneously formed soft parts
measurable_quantities: fit of logarithmic spiral to organic outlines; mode of growth (accretionary versus simultaneous)
candidate_data: Outline and surface datasets of shells, horns and claws (MorphoSource) compared with leaf-outline and fish-shape image datasets.

section: Measuring the spiral of the shell
label: Whorl breadths of nautiloid, ammonitoid and gastropod shells form a geometric progression
measurable_quantities: breadths of successive whorls along a radius vector; whorl expansion rate
candidate_data: Published whorl-expansion-rate measurements of ammonoids and gastropods, and shell CT scans in MorphoSource.

label: All differences of form between shells are differences of degree in a few growth ratios
measurable_quantities: generating-curve shape; whorl expansion rate; translation rate along the axis; distance of generating curve from axis
candidate_data: Theoretical-morphospace analyses of real shells using Raupian coiling parameters, fitted to shell scans from MorphoSource or museum image collections.

label: The constant angle of nautiloid, ammonitoid and gastropod spirals is about 80°–85°
measurable_quantities: spiral constant angle; ratio of breadths of successive whorls
candidate_data: Published Raupian coiling-parameter (whorl expansion rate) compilations for ammonoids and gastropods, and MorphoSource shell scans.

label: Separation or overlap of whorls reflects the growth-rate ratio of outer to inner border
measurable_quantities: inner versus outer whorl radius on the same radius vector; degree of whorl overlap or umbilical width
candidate_data: Ammonoid and nautiloid coiling-parameter datasets (whorl overlap, umbilical ratio) and shell CT scans in MorphoSource.

label: Spiral constants of shells give no valid evidence of ancestry
measurable_quantities: spiral angle or coiling parameters; stratigraphic first-appearance age; phylogenetic position
candidate_data: Paleobiology Database occurrence ages combined with cephalopod coiling-parameter datasets and published cephalopod phylogenies.

label: Mathematical morphology can reveal orthogenetic series and warn of convergence
measurable_quantities: coiling parameters through stratigraphic sequences; frequency of convergent shell forms across clades
candidate_data: Paleobiology Database stratigraphic data combined with shell morphometrics, and phylogenies for convergence analysis.

section: Changes of spiral angle with age
label: Ontogenetic change in spiral angle explains narrowing-whorled and uncoiling ammonites
measurable_quantities: spiral angle or whorl expansion rate as a function of whorl number
candidate_data: Ontogenetic coiling measurements of heteromorph ammonoids from published morphometric studies and MorphoSource fossil scans.

label: Dissimilar turbinate shells share similar spiral angles and differ mainly in apical angle
measurable_quantities: spiral angle; apical semi-angle of the enveloping cone; ratio of breadths of successive whorls
candidate_data: Gastropod shell morphometric datasets with coiling parameters (whorl expansion rate and translation rate) and shell scans in MorphoSource.

label: Bivalve growth lines are coaxial curves set by direction-dependent growth rate
measurable_quantities: shape of successive growth lines; radial growth increment as a function of direction from the umbo
candidate_data: Outline and growth-line images of bivalve shells from museum collections and sclerochronology studies; elliptic Fourier outline datasets.

label: Incomplete moulting gives Estheria a mollusc-like spiral shell with growth lines
measurable_quantities: number of growth lines versus number of moults; ratio of successive growth-line sizes
candidate_data: Published morphometric studies of clam shrimp (Spinicaudata) carapace growth lines and museum specimen images.

label: Brachiopod spiral arm direction follows shell shape through spatial constraint
measurable_quantities: shell width-to-length ratio; direction and shape of spiralia
candidate_data: Paleobiology Database brachiopod occurrences with shell-shape measurements and published serial-section or CT reconstructions of brachidia.

label: Ammonite shell and aptychus are two parts of a once united split cone
measurable_quantities: developmental origin of aptychi and cephalopod shells; homology of dorsal and ventral shell fields
candidate_data: Developmental and histological studies of cephalopod shell fields and ammonoid aptychi, and molecular phylogenies of Cephalopoda; none known as a dedicated dataset.

label: Cephalopod septa take the form of minimal surfaces like soap films
measurable_quantities: septal surface curvature; mean curvature constancy across the septum; septal attachment line geometry
candidate_data: Micro-CT reconstructions of Nautilus and ammonoid septa (e.g. MorphoSource) analysed for mean curvature.

label: The fine frilling of ammonite sutures is a surface-tension phenomenon
measurable_quantities: fractal dimension or complexity of suture lines; shape of terminal suture elements
candidate_data: Published ammonoid suture-complexity (fractal dimension) datasets and digitised suture lines, compared with viscous-fingering patterns.

label: The same spiral shell forms recur across unrelated groups, all ages and all seas
measurable_quantities: coiling parameters by clade, geological period and environment
candidate_data: Paleobiology Database occurrences with environment and age, combined with shell coiling-parameter datasets and OBIS/GBIF distribution records.

label: Natural Selection plays no necessary part in producing spiral shell forms
measurable_quantities: association between coiling parameters and fitness or ecological performance; shell-form disparity relative to adaptive expectations
candidate_data: Functional-morphology and hydrodynamic studies of shell coiling, with Paleobiology Database survivorship data; none known that directly settles the question.

label: Single-chambered foraminiferal shells take the form of fluid drops under surface tension
measurable_quantities: chamber shape and curvature; deviation from equilibrium drop profiles
candidate_data: 3D micro-CT and image collections of foraminiferal tests such as the Endless Forams image set and MorphoSource scans, compared with computed drop shapes.

label: Foraminifera are spiral because they grow by permanent increments added outside
measurable_quantities: chamber addition sequence; coiling geometry of the test
candidate_data: Micro-CT ontogenetic reconstructions of foraminiferal tests published on MorphoSource and Dryad.

label: Septa are convex outwards in Foraminifera and concave in Nautilus because of pressure side
measurable_quantities: sign and magnitude of septal curvature; septal surface area relative to bounding contour
candidate_data: Micro-CT scans of foraminifera and Nautilus shells on MorphoSource.

label: Spiral foraminiferal shells are logarithmic spirals, large shells similar to small ones
measurable_quantities: radius of successive whorls versus vectorial angle; shape of juvenile versus adult test
candidate_data: Micro-CT data of planispiral and trochospiral foraminifera on MorphoSource; published chamber-by-chamber morphometric datasets on Dryad.

label: Fusulina whorls increase in ratio 1:1.5, a spiral of constant angle about 86°
measurable_quantities: whorl breadth; whorl expansion ratio; spiral constant angle
candidate_data: Thin-section morphometric data on fusulinids in the paleontological literature and specimen records in the Paleobiology Database.

label: Constant chamber-size ratio follows from growth proportional to existing mass
measurable_quantities: volume of successive chambers; cumulative test volume; chamber volume ratio
candidate_data: Micro-CT chamber volume series for planktonic foraminifera published on Dryad and MorphoSource.

label: Minimum potential energy plus proportional growth yields the logarithmic spiral
measurable_quantities: chamber shape similarity; chamber position relative to predecessors; contact angles at sutures
candidate_data: Micro-CT chamber reconstructions of foraminifera compared with physical simulations of sequential drop accretion.

label: Attached Foraminifera form plane spirals with whorls flattened on the attached side
measurable_quantities: coiling mode (planispiral or trochospiral); life habit (attached, free benthic, planktonic); whorl flattening
candidate_data: Foraminiferal trait compilations (life habit and coiling mode) such as the Triton planktonic foraminifera dataset and the World Foraminifera Database.

section: Variability and the constancy of species
label: Many foraminiferal species and genera may be temporary manifestations of variability
measurable_quantities: morphological variation within populations; ecophenotypic response of shell form to environment; genetic distinctness of morphospecies
candidate_data: Molecular barcoding studies of foraminiferal morphospecies (e.g. the PFR2 Planktonic Foraminifera Ribosomal Reference database) and culture experiments on ecophenotypic variation.

label: Foraminiferal forms follow such simple laws that none is fitter than another to survive
measurable_quantities: morphospecies longevity; relationship between test morphology and extinction or survival
candidate_data: Fossil occurrence data for foraminifera in the Paleobiology Database and the Neptune (NSB) database, linked to morphological traits.

label: Identical foraminiferal forms may have arisen independently again and again
measurable_quantities: frequency of homeomorphy between unrelated lineages; phylogenetic distribution of morphotypes
candidate_data: Morphology-calibrated phylogenies of planktonic foraminifera (e.g. Aze et al. 2011 Macroperforate phylogeny), the Triton dataset and molecular phylogenies.

section: Strength as a supposed selective factor
label: Increased shell strength is not an advantage driving foraminiferal evolution
measurable_quantities: breakage frequency of tests in death assemblages; mechanical strength of tests of differing complexity; survivorship by morphotype
candidate_data: Taphonomic fragmentation studies of foraminiferal assemblages and mechanical testing studies of tests (e.g. finite-element analyses published on Dryad).

section: Strength as a supposed selective factor
label: Foraminifera are absent from coarse gravels because of hydraulic sorting by currents
measurable_quantities: sediment grain size; bottom current velocity; foraminiferal test abundance and size
candidate_data: Seafloor sediment surveys with grain size and foraminiferal counts (e.g. the ForCenS census database and PANGAEA sediment datasets).

label: Forms set by physical forces undermine inference of kinship from similarity
candidate_data: none known

label: Rhinoceros horn is a plane logarithmic spiral from constant front-to-back growth ratio
